title: Squash Commits
summary: Turns a messy branch history into a few clear commits with proper messages, showing the plan before rewriting anything.
description: Work in progress leaves commits named "fix" or "again" that make review and later debugging harder. This command groups the commits on your branch into logical units and drafts a message for each.
It shows the plan and a backup point first, rewrites only after your yes, and warns you before touching commits that other people may already have.
useWhen: Before opening a pull request from a branch full of throwaway commits
A review asked you to clean up the history
You want one commit per logical change for an easy revert
You are tidying a branch before a merge to main
body:
Squash the commits on this branch. Instructions: $ARGUMENTS (for example the base branch or "single commit").

1. Find the base: `git merge-base HEAD <base>` with the given base or the default branch. Show `git log --oneline <base>..HEAD` and `git diff --stat <base>..HEAD`.
2. If any of these commits exist on a shared remote branch that others may use, warn and ask before continuing.
3. Propose groups: related commits by files and purpose, ordered so each group builds and passes tests alone. Give each a message in the project's style (check recent `git log -n 10 --oneline`), with a body explaining why.
4. Print the plan: new commit message, commits folded into it, files.
5. Create a backup: `git branch backup/<branch>-<date>`.
6. After approval, rewrite without interactive tools: `git reset --soft <base>` then commit each group by staging its files, or a scripted `git rebase`. Verify `git diff backup/<branch>` is empty.

Report the new log and the backup name. Do not push; mention that `--force-with-lease` is required if already pushed.

example.result:
11 commits since main. Plan:
1. feat(search): add fuzzy matching (6 commits)
2. test(search): cover empty and unicode queries (3)
3. docs: describe search flags (2)
Backup: backup/search-1115. Proceed?
After yes: new log shown, diff against backup is empty.

faq.question: Can I get back the old history?
faq.answer: Yes. A backup branch is created before any rewrite, and the final check proves the result matches it exactly.

faq.question: Does it force push?
faq.answer: Never. It tells you when a force push with lease is needed and leaves that to you.

access: Rewrites local commits after you approve the plan, with a backup branch
